clue.text: Chauvinism appears to lose vigour, faltering when sovereign leaves

parts.note: to flag is to tire or lose vigour

indicators.note: the sovereign leaves, so its letter is taken out of the word for faltering

parts.note: faltering means wavering, hesitating
R stands for Rex or Regina, the reigning sovereign

explanation.surface: Jingoism seems to be running out of steam, wobbling once the monarch departs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when sovereign leaves' removes the R (Rex, Regina) from the word for faltering, giving WAVING; 'appears to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Showy waving of the national banner stands for aggressive, boastful patriotism, which is what chauvinism originally meant.

clue.text: City left a hero in the lurch

indicators.note: in the lurch suggests the letters of a hero are left stranded and jumbled

explanation.surface: A man abandoned a hero when he needed help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the lurch' signals an anagram of A HERO, giving AHORE after L.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a major city in Pakistan, capital of Punjab province.

clue.text: Woolly animal

definitions.meaning: a woolly is a knitted sweater; this one is a fisherman's jersey
a breed of dairy cattle from the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: A sheep, perhaps, described as fleecy.
explanation.walkthrough: Woolly looks like an adjective for the animal; it is a noun, a woollen jumper. A jumper is a sweater.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick knitted fisherman's jumper, and a breed of dairy cow, both named after the Channel Island.

clue.text: Employed by thousands of orthodontists, etc

indicators.note: employed by says the letters are taken up within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Used by many dental specialists, and the like.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across thousANDS OF ORTHodontists.
explanation.definitionFit: Etcetera is Latin for 'and the rest', which this phrase says in English.

clue.text: I am to turn out better

parts.note: I'm is short for I am
to prove is to turn out, as in it proved true

explanation.surface: My goal is to come out of this a stronger person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' is a verb here: to make or become better.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something superior is to upgrade or enhance it.

clue.text: One wet spot turns up in the desert

indicators.note: turns up in a down clue means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a bog is a wet, marshy spot

explanation.surface: A single damp patch appears in an arid wasteland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses the whole run I + BOG, read upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the great arid region spanning Mongolia and northern China.

clue.text: Kills after argument and scrap escalate

indicators.note: escalate means go up, so in this down clue the letters are read upwards

parts.note: a set-to is an argument or fight
a rag is a scrap of cloth

explanation.surface: A row and a brawl get out of hand and end in murder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'escalate' reverses SET-TO + RAG as a whole, reading it upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: This verb means strangles with a cord or wire, a way of putting someone to death.

clue.text: He searched all over the place — no luck

indicators.note: all over the place means the letters of he searched are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A man hunted everywhere and came up empty.
explanation.walkthrough: HARD CHEESE is British slang for bad luck, often said with little sympathy.
explanation.definitionFit: This British slang expression means tough luck or bad fortune.

clue.text: Capital providing a Scottish engineer with zero return

indicators.note: return means the whole string a, engineer and zero is read backwards

parts.note: James Watt, the Scottish engineer who improved the steam engine
zero looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A city that gives a Scots engineer nothing back for his efforts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns the whole run A + WATT + O, read backwards, into the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the capital city of Canada.

clue.text: Being ill, he sipped a therapeutic liquid

indicators.note: being ill suggests the letters of he sipped are out of sorts and rearranged

explanation.surface: Feeling poorly, a man takes a sip of some medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being ill' signals an anagram of HE SIPPED.
explanation.definitionFit: Farmers plunge flocks into this disinfecting bath to kill parasites, so it is a treatment liquid for wool-bearing livestock.

clue.text: One way to travel to Shanghai

definitions.meaning: in American usage a railway, a means of travelling by train
to shanghai someone is to force or coerce them into something

explanation.surface: A route for getting to the Chinese city.
explanation.walkthrough: Shanghai looks like the destination, but it is a verb: to force someone into doing something, as sailors were once kidnapped onto ships.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway line is a way of travelling, and to push someone through or coerce them is also to railroad them.

clue.text: County borders

definitions.meaning: short for Bedfordshire, an English county
borders are strips of garden planted with flowers

explanation.surface: The boundaries of a shire.
explanation.walkthrough: Bedfordshire, an English county north of London, is abbreviated as Beds; garden borders are flower beds.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviated name of Bedfordshire, and garden plots along a lawn edge planted with flowers.

clue.text: Dictator opposed by Winston

definitions.meaning: an all-powerful ruler watching over everyone
Winston Smith rebels against the Party's leader in Orwell's novel 1984

explanation.surface: A tyrant resisted by Churchill.
explanation.walkthrough: Winston suggests Churchill, who opposed real dictators; this one is the leader Winston Smith defies in George Orwell's 1984.
explanation.definitionFit: The figurehead of the Party in Orwell's 1984, a totalitarian leader whom the hero Winston Smith secretly resists.

clue.text: Take iron to very short, shot — the excitement's intense

definitions.note: a phrase describing a state of intense excitement, standing for the noun

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: short means the word very loses its final letter

parts.note: a shot or throw is a pitch

explanation.surface: A golfer's instruction: use an iron for a very short shot when the tension mounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts very to VER. The surface reads like golf, with iron a club, but iron is FE.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase names the peak of agitation or enthusiasm, as in a crowd roaring at a cup final.

clue.text: Carpet beater may cause turmoil

definitions.meaning: beating a rug literally stirs up a cloud of particles
idiom for creating a commotion or fuss

explanation.surface: A rug beater might create chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally what beating a rug does to its grime, and idiomatically to stir up a fuss or commotion.

clue.text: Run into chap before 8

indicators.note: into means the run letter goes inside the word for chap

parts.note: a chap is a guy
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Sprint up to a fellow ahead of eight o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 refers to 8 down, HARD CHEESE, which this answer is an example of.
explanation.definitionFit: This Swiss cheese is a firm, pressed variety, a classic example of a hard cheese.

clue.text: Serving no purpose, being impotent without America

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the word for impotent goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: impotent means powerless, unable
US is short for the United States

explanation.surface: Useless, being powerless without American help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, so America sits inside the word for impotent rather than being dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that cannot be put to work is of no use.

clue.text: Trick could result in penalty points

parts.note: a fine is a monetary penalty
S, S and E are compass points, together making south-south-east

explanation.surface: A misdeed that might earn a driver a penalty on the licence.
explanation.walkthrough: Penalty points suggest a driving licence; here they are a penalty (FINE) and points of the compass (SSE).
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, this is a trick-winning manoeuvre with a lower card, and more broadly any subtle ploy.

clue.text: Prince — he's been ordered to keep things secret

indicators.note: been ordered means the letters of prince and he are put into a new order

parts.note: he's here stands for he, with the 's (has) joining it to the indicator

explanation.surface: A royal has been commanded to stay quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'been ordered' signals an anagram of PRINCE + HE.
explanation.definitionFit: To put a message into code is a way to stop others reading it.

clue.text: Dashing fellow was ahead, but crumpled

parts.note: a buck is a dashing young man
led means was ahead, in front

explanation.surface: A dashing man was leading, but then collapsed.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal that has bent and given way under pressure has crumpled.

clue.text: Put up a bit of a fight at first, delivering a swinging punch

indicators.note: at first says the bit of a fight comes before the word for put up

parts.note: a round is one stage of a boxing match
to put someone up is to house them

explanation.surface: Showed some resistance early on, then landed a big haymaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' puts the bit of a fight ahead, though the clue mentions put up first; a roundhouse is a wild swinging blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild, wide-arcing blow thrown with a sweep of the arm, the kind seen in brawls.

clue.text: An odd character in action

definitions.meaning: an eccentric person, as in he's a real one
a lawsuit, a legal action brought before a court

explanation.surface: An eccentric figure at work.
explanation.definitionFit: An eccentric is called a right one of these, and a lawsuit heard in court is also one.

clue.text: A measure of acidity in dry field

indicators.note: in means the acidity measure is placed inside the word for dry

parts.note: sere means dry or withered
pH is the scale measuring acidity

explanation.surface: A farmer testing the acidity of soil in a parched field.
explanation.walkthrough: Field is an area of activity or interest, not farmland.
explanation.definitionFit: Domain or area of activity, as in her field of expertise.

clue.text: The rest of the wood cut by Jack and Ray

indicators.note: cut by means the wood is split open and the other letters go inside it

parts.note: teak is a hard wood
a jack or jack tar is a sailor, an AB (able seaman)
ray, or re, is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: The rest of the timber being sawn by two workmen named Jack and Ray.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack and Ray look like two workmen's names; a jack (tar) is a sailor, and ray is the sol-fa note from 'Do-Re-Mi'. 'cut by' puts them inside the wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A short pause from work, a breather taken over a cuppa.

clue.text: Part of "The Cruel Sea" in colour

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A scene from the war film The Cruel Sea, shot in colour.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took the definition as Sea" in colour; the definition is colour, with in a link, and the run thE CRUel sits inside the film title.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale greyish-yellow shade, the hue of unbleached linen.

clue.text: Afterwards admitting an expression of disgust, as well as one of joy

indicators.note: admitting means the word for afterwards lets the exclamation in

parts.note: later means afterwards
ugh is the exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: Then letting out a cry of revulsion, along with a cry of delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one of joy' means an expression of joy, picking up the earlier 'expression'.
explanation.definitionFit: Merriment shows itself in this sound, so it is an outward expression of happiness.

clue.text: Note invested in round seed cake

indicators.note: invested in means the note is clothed by, placed inside, the other letters
round means the word for seed is turned about and read backwards

parts.note: rice is the seed of a cereal grass
la is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A banknote put into a round seed cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' turns the seed backwards to ECIR, and 'invested in' clothes the note with it. Seed cake looks like one item; the definition is just cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A long choux pastry filled with cream and topped with chocolate, a type of small cake.

clue.text: Persevering man retired after one from Paris slipped up

indicators.note: after places the man's reversed name behind the French word

parts.note: un is French for one

indicators.note: retired means the name is drawn back, read backwards

parts.note: Ted is a man's name
erred means slipped up, made a mistake

explanation.surface: A man who stuck at it retired after a Frenchman blundered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns the man's name back to DET, and 'after' sets it behind the French word for one; the slip follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Not put off or discouraged, so carrying on resolutely.
